entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: citsvābhāvyād asau devaḥ svātmanā vimṛṣan prabhuḥ | anāśritādibhūmyantā bhūmikāḥ pratipadyate
entries.translation: From nature of consciousness, that god by own self reflecting — Lord, from unattached to end-of-stages — stages attains.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. dative singular — the recipient
entries.sanskrit: samastalakṣanāyoga eva yasyopalakṣaṇam tasmai namo 'stu devāya kasmai cid api śambhave
entries.translation: To the god — to gracious someone — for whom the meeting of all marks is itself the mark — bow.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. neuter singular — nominative and accusative share the form
entries.sanskrit: bhaktikṣobhavaśād īśa svātmabhūte 'rcanaṃ tvayi citraṃ dainyāya no yāvad dīnatāyāḥ paraṃ phalam
entries.translation: By devotion-agitation, worship in self-become-Him — wonder: poverty's top fruit is lowliness' fruit.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: tad eva śyānatāṃ yātaṃ bhāvarūpair vibhāvyate | svātmā maheśvaro devaḥ krīḍate parameśvaraḥ
entries.translation: That indeed gone to quiescence, by being-forms manifested — own self, great Lord, god plays, supreme Lord.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: iti śakticakrayantraṃ krīḍāyogena vāhayan devaḥ | aham eva śuddharūpaḥ śaktimahācakranāyakapadasthaḥ
entries.translation: Thus driving, by play-discipline, the power-wheel-machine — god: I indeed, pure-formed, standing in the power-great-wheel-lord-seat.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: ātmā mama bhavadbhaktisudhāpānayuvāpi san lokayātrārajorāgāt palitair iva dhūsaraḥ
entries.translation: My self stays young, drinking the nectar of Your devotion — though greyed as if with the dust of worldly journeying and its passions.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. accusative singular — the object
entries.sanskrit: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ | prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya
entries.translation: Own-light made, speech-goddess, sense-flowers-offering-arranged — first-unfolding guru, then venerated, heart entered.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: anantānandasarasī devī priyatamā yathā aviyuktāsti te tadvad ekā tvadbhaktir astu me
entries.translation: As the lake of endless bliss, the Goddess, the beloved, is inseparable from You — so may one devotion of mine be inseparable.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. neuter singular — nominative and accusative share the form
entries.sanskrit: citraṃ nisargato nātha duḥkhabījam idaṃ manaḥ tvadbhaktirasasaṃsiktam niḥśreyasamahāphalam
entries.translation: A wonder, Lord: this mind, by nature pain's seed — watered by the essence of devotion to You, becomes liberation's great fruit.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. genitive singular — the possessor
entries.translation: Not uninterruptedness — for it misses relation: if it were so, it would hold of iron bars. Hence fusion of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. accusative singular — the object
entries.sanskrit: ādyantāntargatānantaśaktiviśrāntinirbharām anuccāryām | ahaṃ vācam adhīye hṛdayaṃ vibhoḥ
entries.translation: Filled with rest of beginning-end-entered endless power — unspeakable — I study speech: the Lord's heart.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative plural — the subjects (vocative shares the form)
entries.translation: Of-Shambhu undivided hearts victorious gurus formerly — without-rising absorption obtained end prosperity.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject (vocative shares the form)
entries.sanskrit: sādṛśaiḥ kiṃ na carvyeta bhavadbhaktimahauṣadhiḥ tādṛśī bhagavan yasyā mokṣākhyo 'nantaro rasaḥ
entries.translation: Why would people like me not chew Your devotion's great medicine — whose after-taste, O Lord, is called liberation?

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: dāsasya me prasīdatu bhagavān etāvad eva nanu yāce dātā tribhuvananātho yasya na tanmādṛśāṃ dṛśo viṣayaḥ
entries.translation: May the Lord be pleased with me, His slave — I ask only this, since the three-worlds Giver exceeds my sight.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. ablative or genitive singular — the two share the form
entries.sanskrit: madhunaḥ samavekṣya kālatāṃ bhramaraś cumbati yūthikālatām
entries.translation: Having observed honey's season, the bee kisses the yūthikā creeper.

entries.note: Hard text. Find the form you know — the rest is for later. nominative singular — the subject
entries.sanskrit: viṣayeṣu sārvabhaumaḥ sarvajanaiḥ pūjyate yathā rājā | bhuvaneṣu sarvadaivair yogabhraṣṭas tathā pūjyaḥ
entries.translation: As an emperor among things is honored by all people as king, so among worlds the yoga-fallen is honored by all gods.
